provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Artist study
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different art forms.
The pupils should be able to describe feelings about artworks.

Introduction:
We have seen many beautiful things around us.
Today we will look at art made by Nigerian artists.

Content:
An artist is someone who makes art.
We can see paintings, drawings and sculptures.
Look at the picture of this artist's work.
What do you see?
How does it make you feel?

Class activity:
Pass around pictures of local artworks.
Each child says what they see and how they feel.

Evaluation questions:
What is an artist?
What do you see in this picture?
How does this art make you feel?

Summary:
Today we learned about artists and their work.

topics.title: Sketch books start
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a simple sketch book.
The pupils should be able to make daily drawings.

Introduction:
We have seen how artists make art.
Today we will make our own sketch books.

Content:
A sketch book is a book for drawing.
We can use paper to make our own.
Fold paper in half to make pages.
Staple the sides to bind your book.
Draw something small every day.

Class activity:
Each child makes their own sketch book.
They draw one thing they like inside.

Evaluation questions:
What is a sketch book?
How do we make a sketch book?
What did you draw today?

Summary:
We made our own sketch books for drawing.

topics.title: Perspective first step
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain near and far in art.
The pupils should be able to draw a road to their house.

Introduction:
We know things look different from far away.
Today we learn to show this in our drawings.

Content:
Things that are near look big.
Things that are far look small.
When we draw a road, it gets smaller at the end.
This is called perspective.
Let's draw a road to our house.

Class activity:
Children draw a road getting smaller at the end.
Add houses and trees along the road.

Evaluation questions:
What do near things look like?
What do far things look like?
Draw a road getting smaller.

Summary:
We learned to show near and far in our drawings.

topics.title: Clay technique
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate pinch, coil and slab methods.
The pupils should be able to choose a technique for their project.

Introduction:\Today we will play with clay.
We will learn different ways to shape clay.

Content:
Clay is soft mud we can shape.
Pinch method: squeeze clay with fingers.
Coil method: roll clay into long ropes.
Slab method: flatten clay into flat pieces.
Choose which method you like best.

Class activity:
Children explore clay with each technique.
They make a small object using their chosen method.

Evaluation questions:
What is the pinch method?
What is the coil method?
What did you make with clay?

Summary:
We learned three ways to shape clay.

topics.title: Textile patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify adire, ankara and aso oke.
The pupils should be able to design their own cloth pattern.

Introduction:
We have seen beautiful Nigerian fabrics.
Today we will learn about their patterns.

Content:
Adire is tie - dyed cloth with patterns.
Ankara is bright printed cloth.
Aso oke is hand - woven cloth.
Each pattern tells a story.
Let's design our own cloth pattern.

Class activity:
Children draw their own cloth pattern using bright colors.
They can use shapes and lines like Nigerian fabrics.

Evaluation questions:
What is adire?
What is ankara?
What pattern did you design?

Summary:
We learned about Nigerian fabrics and made our own patterns.

topics.title: Printing mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate stamp, rub and screen printing.
The pupils should be able to create a repeating pattern.

Introduction:
We have made drawings and patterns.
Today we will learn to print our designs.

Content:
Printing is making many copies of a design.
Stamp printing: press a shape into paint.
Rub printing: place paper on textured surface and rub.
Screen printing: push paint through a screen with holes.
We can make patterns by repeating our prints.

Class activity:
Children choose a printing method.
They make a pattern by repeating their print design.

Evaluation questions:
What is stamp printing?
What is rub printing?
How do we make a pattern with printing?

Summary:
We learned different ways to print and make patterns.

topics.title: 3D craft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a paper animal sculpture.
The pupils should be able to use fold, roll and paste techniques.

Introduction:
We have made flat drawings and prints.
Today we will make things that stand up.

Content:
3D art has height, width and depth.
We can make 3D animals with paper.
Fold paper to make shapes.
Roll paper to make tubes.
Paste pieces together to build.

Class activity:
Children create a paper animal using fold, roll and paste.
They add details like eyes and patterns.

Evaluation questions:
What is 3D art?
What three techniques did we use?
What animal did you make?

Summary:
We made 3D paper animals using paper techniques.

topics.title: Portrait mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw a portrait of a loved adult.
The pupils should be able to practice proportion in drawing.

Introduction:
We have drawn animals and objects.
Today we will draw people we love.

Content:
A portrait is a drawing of a person.
When we draw people, heads are round.
Bodies are bigger than heads.
Arms and legs connect to the body.
Let's draw someone we love.

Class activity:
Children draw a portrait of a grown - up they love.
They practice getting the proportions right.

Evaluation questions:
What is a portrait?
What shape is a head?
Who did you draw and why?

Summary:
We practiced drawing people we love.

topics.title: Group installation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plan a group art project.
The pupils should be able to contribute to a large artwork.

Introduction:
We have made many individual artworks.
Today we will work together on one big piece.

Content:
An installation is a large art piece.
We plan together what to make.
Each child does a part.
We put all parts together to make one big artwork.

Class activity:
The class plans and builds a paper forest installation.
Each child makes trees, animals or plants to add.

Evaluation questions:
What is an art installation?
What did you contribute to our project?
How did we work together?

Summary:
We created a big artwork together as a class.

topics.title: Exhibition opening
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to curate a class gallery.
The pupils should be able to create invitation cards.

Introduction:
We have made many beautiful artworks.
Today we will show them in an exhibition.

Content:
An exhibition is showing art to others.
We arrange our artworks nicely on walls.
We make invitation cards for parents.
The cards tell when and where to come see our art.

Class activity:
Children arrange their artworks around the classroom.
They make colorful invitation cards for their parents.

Evaluation questions:
What is an art exhibition?
What did you put in our exhibition?
Who will you invite to see our art?

Summary:
We prepared our art exhibition and invited our parents.
